name: Merge PDFs
short: Stitch several PDFs into one file.
desc: Add your PDFs, put them in the order you want, and download a single combined file.

inputs.label: PDFs to merge
inputs.hint: Use the arrows to change the order.

tips: Files are joined top to bottom, exactly as listed.
Want to interleave pages instead? Try “Weave two PDFs”.

faq.q: Is there a limit on how many files I can merge?
faq.a: Not one we set. The practical limit is your device’s memory, so very large batches may be slow.

faq.q: Will bookmarks and links survive?
faq.a: Page content is kept. Bookmarks and document-level links from the originals are not carried over.

name: Weave two PDFs
short: Interleave pages, handy for double-sided scans.
desc: Alternate pages from two PDFs: A1, B1, A2, B2… Perfect when your scanner did fronts and backs separately.

options.label: Second file is in reverse order
options.hint: Most sheet-fed scanners give you the backs last-to-first.

faq.q: The two files have different page counts.
faq.a: Pages are woven until one file runs out; the leftover pages of the longer file go at the end.

name: Split a PDF
short: Cut one PDF into several, by range or size.
desc: Break a PDF into separate files: custom ranges, every N pages, or one file per page.

options.label: Ranges
options.hint: Each comma-separated range becomes its own file.

tips: Several outputs? Use “Download all (ZIP)” on the results.

name: Pull out pages
short: Keep only the pages you pick.
desc: Type the pages you want and get a new PDF containing just those, in the order you typed them.

options.label: Pages to keep
options.hint: Also works: odd, even, first, last.

name: Delete pages
short: Drop the pages you do not need.
desc: List the pages to throw away and download what is left.

name: Reorder pages
short: Type the new page order.
desc: Write the pages in the order you want, e.g. 3, 1, 2-5. Repeat a number to duplicate a page. Leave one out to drop it.

options.label: New order
options.hint: Pages you do not list are left out.

name: Flip page order
short: Last page first.
desc: Reverse the whole document so the last page becomes the first.

name: Rotate pages
short: Turn pages 90°, 180° or 270°.
desc: Fix sideways or upside-down scans. Rotate every page, or only the ones you name.

name: Add blank pages
short: Slip empty pages in where you need them.
desc: Insert one or more blank pages before or after the pages you choose, handy for double-sided printing or notes.

name: Change page size
short: Fit every page onto A4, Letter and friends.
desc: Scale pages to a standard paper size. Content is shrunk or enlarged to fit and centred, never stretched.
tips: Landscape pages stay landscape.

name: Trim margins
short: Crop white space off the edges.
desc: Cut a fixed amount off the top, right, bottom and left of the pages you choose.

name: Print several per sheet
short: 2, 4, 6 or 9 pages on one sheet.
desc: Shrink pages and tile them onto bigger sheets, great for handouts, proofs and saving paper.

options.label: Draw a thin border around each page

name: Repair a PDF
short: Rebuild a damaged file.
desc: Tries to open a broken PDF, rescue every page it can read, and write them into a clean new file.
tips: If a page is truly destroyed, it cannot be brought back.

name: Number the pages
short: Add page numbers anywhere on the page.
desc: Stamp “Page 3 of 12” (or any format you like) on every page, or just some of them.

options.label: Format
options.hint: Use {n} for the number and {total} for the page count.

tips: Skip a cover page by entering 2-last in “Only these pages”, and set “First number” to 1 or 2 as you like.

name: Text watermark
short: Stamp DRAFT, CONFIDENTIAL or anything else.
desc: Place a big, translucent text stamp across your pages: centred, or tiled over the whole page.

name: Logo or image stamp
short: Place a logo or signature image on pages.
desc: Put a PNG or JPG, such as a logo, stamp or scanned signature, on your pages with adjustable size and transparency.

name: Headers & footers
short: Repeat text at the top and bottom of pages.
desc: Add left, centre and right text to the header and footer of every page. Use {n}, {total}, {date} and {file} as placeholders.

name: Write on a PDF
short: Place a line of text anywhere on a page.
desc: Type a note, a date or a name and put it exactly where you want it, using percentages from the top-left corner.
tips: This adds new text on top. It does not edit text that is already in the PDF.

name: Photos to PDF
short: Turn JPG, PNG or WebP images into a PDF.
desc: Drop in your pictures, order them, and get one PDF. Big phone photos are shrunk by default so the file stays a sensible size.

inputs.label: Images
inputs.hint: Use the arrows to change the order.

options.label: Shrink very large photos
options.hint: Recommended. Caps the longest side at 2200 px.

name: Scan to PDF
short: Camera or photos in, clean document out.
desc: Take pictures of paper documents (or choose existing photos) and turn them into a tidy PDF with the shadows evened out.

inputs.label: Photos of your pages
inputs.hint: On a phone this opens the camera.

name: Text or Markdown to PDF
short: Write or paste text, get a neat PDF.
desc: Paste plain text or Markdown (headings, lists, quotes, code blocks, rules) and turn it into a clean, printable PDF.
tips: Characters outside Latin-1 (like emoji or non-Latin scripts) show up as “?”.

name: PDF to pictures
short: Save every page as a JPG or PNG.
desc: Render pages to high-quality images, in a ZIP or one by one. Pick the resolution that suits your use.
tips: 300 dpi pages can be large. Convert fewer pages at a time if your browser struggles.

name: Copy text out
short: Pull the text from a PDF.
desc: Extract the selectable text from a PDF so you can copy it or save it as a .txt file.
tips: A scanned PDF is really a picture, so it has no text to copy. OCR for scans is on the roadmap.

name: Make it smaller
short: Shrink the file size of a PDF.
desc: Reduce a PDF so it fits an email or an upload limit. Choose a gentle clean-up that keeps text, or a stronger squeeze that flattens pages to pictures.

options.label: How hard to squeeze
options.hint: Balanced, Strong and Tiny turn each page into a compressed image, so text can no longer be selected.

tips: Start with Gentle. If that is not small enough, move up a level.
PDFs that are mostly text rarely get much smaller; scans and photo-heavy files shrink a lot.

faq.q: Why did my file barely change?
faq.a: Gentle mode only tidies the file structure. If the size is dominated by images, use Balanced or Strong.

name: Grayscale & dark mode
short: Black & white, inverted, sepia or crisp scan look.
desc: Recolour a PDF: save ink with grayscale, read at night with an inverted version, or make a faint scan crisp and high-contrast.
tips: The result is made of page images, so text is no longer selectable.

name: Inspect a PDF
short: See what is hiding inside: metadata, size, forms.
desc: A quick report: page count and sizes, document properties, whether it has hidden metadata, annotations or form fields, and what you may want to clean before sharing.

name: Clean & edit properties
short: Edit title/author, or wipe all metadata.
desc: Change a PDF’s title, author and other properties, or strip every piece of metadata before sending it on.

options.label: Remove all metadata
options.hint: Clears title, author, subject, keywords, software, dates and hidden XMP data.

tips: Blank boxes leave that property unchanged.

name: Flatten forms
short: Lock in form answers and strip comments.
desc: Turn fillable form fields into plain page content so answers can’t be edited, and optionally remove comments and highlights.

name: Black out text
short: Permanently hide words, numbers or patterns.
desc: Type the words you need to hide (one per line). Pages are redrawn with black boxes over every match and saved as pictures, so the hidden text is truly gone.

options.label: Text to black out (one per line)

warn: Always check the result before sharing. Text split across lines, or inside images, may not be found automatically.
tips: Only PDFs with a text layer can be searched. Scans have none.
The result is page images, so no hidden text can be copied out of it.

name: Spot the differences
short: Compare the text of two PDFs.
desc: Pick an old and a new version of a document and get a page-by-page list of lines that were removed or added.
tips: Compares text only. Layout and image changes are not detected.

name: Summarise with AI
short: A short summary of a long PDF (your own AI key).
desc: Get the gist of a long document in seconds. You bring your own API key from OpenAI, Anthropic or Google, set once in Settings.
warn: Text from your PDF is sent straight to the AI provider you chose in Settings, using your own API key. It does not pass through iDuckPDF’s servers.

name: Ask your PDF
short: Ask a question, get an answer with page references.
desc: Ask anything about a document and get an answer that points to the pages it came from. Uses your own AI key from Settings.

options.label: Your question
options.placeholder: e.g. What is the notice period in this contract?

warn: Text from your PDF is sent straight to the AI provider you chose in Settings, using your own API key. It does not pass through iDuckPDF’s servers.

name: Add a password
short: Encrypt a PDF so it needs a password to open.
desc: Protect a PDF with a password (AES-256) before you share it. The file is encrypted inside your browser tab, so the password and the document never leave your device.

options.label: Password to open the file
options.hint: Anyone who opens the PDF will be asked for this. We cannot recover it for you, so keep a copy somewhere safe.

options.label: Allow copying text and images
options.hint: Restrictions are honoured by most PDF viewers, but they are a courtesy: only the open-password is real security.

tips: Use a long password with several words. Short ones can be guessed.
The result is a new file. Your original is untouched, so keep it somewhere safe.

faq.q: How strong is the protection?
faq.a: The file is encrypted with AES-256, the strongest standard PDF encryption. The strength then depends on your password, so choose a long one.

faq.q: Can you recover a forgotten password?
faq.a: No. The password never leaves your browser, so there is nothing for us to recover. Keep a copy of the original file.

faq.q: Will every PDF app open it?
faq.a: Modern readers (Acrobat, Preview, Chrome, Edge, Firefox) open AES-256 files. Very old software may not.

name: Remove a password
short: Unlock a PDF you have the password for.
desc: Take the password off a PDF you own so it opens freely. You need to know the password: this tool does not guess or break passwords. It also lifts printing and copying restrictions.

options.label: Password
options.placeholder: Leave empty if it opens without one
options.hint: Files that open fine but block printing or copying usually need no password here.

tips: This works only with the correct password. It does not crack or bypass anything.
Only unlock documents you have the right to use.

faq.q: Can you unlock a PDF if I forgot the password?
faq.a: No. This tool needs the password. It cannot guess or break passwords, and nothing is sent anywhere to try.

faq.q: What if the PDF opens but I cannot print or copy?
faq.a: That is a permissions restriction, not an open-password. Leave the password empty and the tool saves a copy without the restrictions.

faq.q: Is my password sent to a server?
faq.a: No. The file is decrypted inside your browser tab, and neither the file nor the password leaves your device.

name: Sign a PDF
short: Draw, type or upload a signature and place it on the page.
desc: Add your signature to a PDF. Draw it with your finger or mouse, type it, or upload a picture, then drag it into place and resize it. Everything happens in your browser tab, so the document and your signature never leave your device.

options.label: Your signature
options.hint: Draw it, type it or upload a picture of it.

options.label: Place it on the page
options.hint: Drag the signature where you want it. Drag the corner, or use the size slider, to resize it.

tips: Your signature is added as a picture. It is a visual signature, not a certified digital one.
To sign in more than one place, run the tool again on the signed copy.

faq.q: Is this a legally binding signature?
faq.a: It is a visual (electronic) signature, which many everyday documents accept. It is not a certificate-based digital signature. Check what the recipient or your local rules require.

faq.q: Is my signature stored or uploaded?
faq.a: No. It is drawn and placed inside your browser tab and is gone when you close it. Nothing is sent to a server.

faq.q: Can I sign more than once on a page?
faq.a: Yes. Download the signed copy and run it through the tool again to add another signature or initials.

name: Fill in a form
short: Type into the fillable fields of a PDF form.
desc: Fill in an interactive PDF form: text boxes, check boxes, drop-downs and radio buttons are listed for you to complete, then saved into a new PDF. Optionally make the answers permanent. Everything stays in your browser.

options.label: Make the answers permanent
options.hint: Turns the fields into ordinary page content so they can no longer be edited. Do this for the copy you send.

tips: Only forms with real fillable fields are listed. For a flat PDF with no fields, use “Write on a PDF” to place text anywhere.
Keep the unflattened copy if you may need to change an answer later.

faq.q: Why does my PDF show no fields?
faq.a: Many PDFs are just pictures of forms. Only PDFs created with interactive fields can be filled this way. For other PDFs, use “Write on a PDF”.

faq.q: What does “make the answers permanent” do?
faq.a: It flattens the form: your answers are merged into the page and the boxes disappear. Flattened forms cannot be edited again.

faq.q: Is my data uploaded?
faq.a: No. The form is read and filled inside your browser tab.

name: Read scans (OCR)
short: Make scanned pages searchable and copyable.
desc: Recognise the text in a scanned PDF or in photos of pages. You get a PDF that looks exactly the same but can be searched, selected and copied, and/or the plain text. The reading happens in your browser, so the scan never leaves your device.

inputs.label: Scanned PDF, or photos of pages
inputs.hint: One PDF, or one or more pictures (JPG, PNG, WebP).

options.label: Language of the text
options.hint: Pick the language the document is written in. The first run downloads about 3 MB for it.

options.label: Skip pages that already have text
options.hint: Pages that are already searchable are left as they are. Turn off to read every page.

tips: Scan at 200 to 300 dpi, straight and in good light. Blurry or crooked pages read poorly.
Check important numbers and names against the original: no OCR is perfect.
It can take several seconds per page. Keep the tab open while it works.

faq.q: Is my scan uploaded?
faq.a: No. The OCR engine runs inside your browser tab. The first time, your browser downloads the engine and the language data from this site, then everything happens on your device.

faq.q: Which languages work?
faq.a: English, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese and Dutch. Other languages need larger fonts and are planned.

faq.q: Will the PDF look different?
faq.a: No. The pages stay exactly as scanned. The recognised text is added underneath as an invisible layer, so you can search and copy it.

faq.q: Why are some words wrong?
faq.a: Handwriting, small print, skewed or low-resolution scans are hard to read. Rescan at a higher resolution, or correct the text file by hand.

name: Word to PDF
short: Convert .docx documents to PDF.
desc: Turn a Word document (.docx) into a PDF: text, headings, lists, tables and pictures, with the document’s own page size and margins. It runs in your browser, so the document is never uploaded. The layout is simplified, so check the result.

inputs.label: Word document (.docx)
inputs.hint: Older .doc files: open them in Word and save as .docx first.

tips: Text, headings, lists, tables, pictures and hyperlinks are kept.
Headers, footers, text boxes, shapes and charts are not reproduced, and fonts become standard PDF fonts, so line breaks can differ from Word.
For a pixel-perfect copy of a complex layout, use Word’s own Save as PDF.

faq.q: Is my document uploaded?
faq.a: No. The .docx is read and converted inside your browser tab. Nothing is sent to a server.

faq.q: Will it look exactly like Word?
faq.a: Not always. It keeps the content and structure, but uses standard PDF fonts and its own line layout, and it does not reproduce headers, footers, text boxes, shapes or charts. Complex or designed documents can look different.

faq.q: What about non-English text?
faq.a: Western European languages work. Other scripts (Greek, Cyrillic, Arabic, Hindi, Chinese, Japanese) cannot be drawn with the standard fonts and appear as question marks.

faq.q: Does it support .doc files?
faq.a: No, only .docx. Open an older .doc in Word and save it as .docx first.

name: Web page to PDF
short: Turn a saved web page or pasted HTML into a PDF.
desc: Convert an HTML file or pasted HTML into a PDF: headings, paragraphs, lists, tables, links and embedded pictures. It runs in your browser, so nothing is uploaded. A web page cannot be fetched by address from here, so save the page first (Ctrl+S) or paste its HTML.

inputs.label: Saved web page (.html), optional
inputs.hint: In your browser press Ctrl+S and choose “Webpage, HTML only”, then add that file. Or paste HTML below.

tips: The page’s style sheets and scripts are ignored: you get the content and structure, not the website’s design.
Pictures are included only when they are embedded in the HTML file itself (data: pictures). Linked pictures are left out.
For an exact copy of a page, use your browser’s Print, then Save as PDF.

faq.q: Can I enter a web address?
faq.a: No. A browser tab cannot read other websites for privacy and security reasons. Save the page (Ctrl+S) or paste its HTML.

faq.q: Why does it not look like the website?
faq.a: Style sheets and scripts are ignored. You get the text, headings, lists, tables and links in a clean layout, which suits articles and documentation.

faq.q: Are pictures included?
faq.a: Only pictures embedded in the HTML as data. Pictures linked from other files or sites are left out.

faq.q: Is my HTML uploaded?
faq.a: No. It is converted inside your browser tab.

name: PDF to Word
short: Get an editable .docx from a PDF.
desc: Convert a PDF into an editable Word document.
reason: Needs server-side layout analysis. Planned with a clear notice that files are sent to be converted.

name: Excel to PDF
short: Spreadsheets to tidy PDFs.
desc: Convert .xlsx and .csv files into PDFs.
reason: Needs a spreadsheet layout engine, so it would run on a server.

name: PDF to Excel
short: Pull tables out into a spreadsheet.
desc: Extract tables from a PDF into .xlsx.
reason: Table detection is hard to do reliably in the browser. Planned on a server.

name: PowerPoint to PDF
short: Slides to PDF.
desc: Turn .pptx presentations into PDFs.
reason: Needs a presentation renderer, so it would run on a server.
